newsitem.title: USA: Reno says FBI, White House had misunderstanding.
newsitem.headline: Reno says FBI, White House had misunderstanding.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno said Wednesday a dispute between the White House and the FBI over a briefing about possible Chinese influence in the 1996 U.S. election campaign was not enough to require appointment of an independent counsel.
"I think there was a misunderstanding," Reno said at a Senate Appropriations subcommittee hearing. "It does not in any way trigger the independent counsel statute."

The Justice Department is investigating possible wrongdoing in Democratic campaign fundraising activities before the 1996 election. But Reno said she had not received any specific, credible evidence of violation of the law that is required before she can ask a court to appoint an independent counsel.

The White House said on Monday that FBI agents briefed members of the National Security Council staff on possible Chinese efforts to influence the election, but told staff members not to pass the information on to President Bill Clinton or other senior officials. The FBI later said it had not put any restrictions on what the NSC staffers could say, but the White House disputed that contention.

"This doesn't concern the campaign finance investigation," Reno said. She said she thought the NSC staffers were told the information was sensitive but there was a misunderstanding over who else could be told about it.

Several members of Congress from both parties are urging Reno to seek an independent counsel to investigate campaign fundraising. She has refused, saying there is not enough evidence of illegal actions to justify the request.
